conviction_note: Small positive lean (p_up 56) on an abs move of 15% (event-implied 14.2%, median reaction 12.3%, raised because the Q3 call last year carried the first next-year outlook): the Q3 revenue bar sits at the midpoint of a guide the company beat by about 3% last quarter, the FY revenue guide was left unchanged while the coding-impact estimate was lowered, the only direct competitor cut its own FY guide on a slower US ramp, and 15.9% of float is short and rising into the print; nothing found is a company number the market has not seen, so the lean stays near 50. impact_sum 3.2 is larger than the scaled 1.8 because each finding is sized alone and several lean the same way on inference.

Adj EPS consensus $0.09 (Benzinga) / $0.11 (Earnings Whispers); company guided Q3 adjusted operating income roughly breakeven. FY2026 guide $835-875M revenue, adj EPS $1.05-1.45 (8-K, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001609550/000160955026000045/insp2026-q2pressreleaseex9.htm); Street FY revenue ~$844M per the Earnings Whispers preview (lower half of guide). No sourced 2027 consensus exists, so any 2027-outlook finding is capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 4,492,372 shares = 15.89% of float, 4.5 days to cover, record date 2026-10-15 (FINRA, published 2026-10-26), up 7.1% from 4,195,817 on 2026-09-30 (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NYSE/INSP/short-interest/). Tape: -6.77% over 5d, -6.42% over 20d, -54% from 52w high, +65% from 52w low; -3.1% intraday on 2026-11-02 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/INSP/). Sell-side Hold consensus, avg target ~$68.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar ($204.1M, two estimate sources agree) sits exactly at the midpoint of the company's -8% to -10% y/y guide ($202.1-206.5M on Q3'25 $224.5M); last quarter the company printed $200.6M against $194.7M consensus (+3.0%) with the coding/WISeR hit at the low end of its own $40-50M range (~$40M), and on the Q2 call said prior-auth submissions (its leading indicator) were rising, a patient backlog was building at centers that paused cases, and the top 25% of centers would be retrained in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-03): revenue +3% vs consensus with an outlook raise, stock +22.83%. Q3 2025 (2025-11-03): revenue $224.5M vs $220.2M, +15.33%. Q1 2026 and Q4 2025 moved on guidance cuts (-12.02%, -12.55%), not on the quarter. A quarter inside the guide has not by itself moved this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The consensus sits at the guide midpoint, i.e. the Street has not modelled the Q2-style beat pattern; if it had, Q3 estimates would sit at or above the top of the range ($206.5M). The stock is down 6.8% over five days into the print and the skew is flat, neither of which looks like a beat being pre-bought. The quarter lands inside what the company guided, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: Same Q2 transcript as the guidance finding below (one document, two lines). Q2 consensus vs actual from the Earnings Whispers / Benzinga records (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/x/INSP). Third-party summary of the Sept 9 Wells Fargo conference says Q2 was the low point with sequential improvement expected in Q3 and Q4 (https://quartr.com/events/inspire-medical-systems-inc-insp-wells-fargo-21st-annual-healthcare-conference_3g6yUiNl, secondary source).

findings.finding: On the Q2 call management lowered its estimate of the full-year coding/WISeR revenue hit to $120-130M and said it would decline sequentially, yet kept the FY revenue range essentially unchanged ($835-875M, low end +$10M only), and an analyst on the call flagged that the lower impact estimate with an unchanged guide implies a cushioned second half; the Street sits at ~$844M, in the lower half, so a raise of the low end/narrowing upward is the plausible guide action and the one line this stock has repeatedly traded on.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line: outlook raise 2026-08-03 +22.83%; guidance cuts 2026-05-04 -12.02%, 2026-02-11 -12.55%, 2025-08-04 -32.35%. Both directions have moved the stock by more than 12%.
findings.why_not_priced: If the market expected a raise, FY consensus would sit at or above the $855M midpoint rather than at ~$844M, and the stock would not have given back 6.8% in the week before the print with 15.9% of float short and rising. The mirror risk (WISeR still in force for Q4, so management holds the range) is filed as its own small negative below.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 call with the reported-quarter finding (one document). Nyxoah's 2026-10-19 prelim, a direct competitor that reported after INSP last spoke, cut its own guide on a slow US ramp, which reduces the share-loss risk to INSP's Q4 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001857190/000110465926117415/tm2627823d1_ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: The Q3 call is where Inspire gave its first next-year outlook last year (Q3 2025: preliminary 2026 growth of 10-11%), and the 2027 backdrop it would guide against includes CMS's proposed CY2027 facility rates for HGNS of $35,414 HOPD (+12%) and $31,722 ASC (+15%) with physician 64582 at $699 (-4%), which management said on the Q2 call it was NOT yet assuming, plus ~$30M of Project Horizon savings to be reinvested in growth; there is no sourced 2027 Street number, so the bar is unknown.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 (2025-11-03), when the preliminary next-year outlook was given: +15.33%. That outlook was later cut (2026-02-11, -12.55%).
findings.why_not_priced: No 2027 revenue consensus is published (searched), so the market has no visible anchor for the first outlook; if the facility-rate increases were priced as upside, a Hold consensus and a ~$68 average target would not sit at spot. Capped small because the bar is unsourced and the CMS final rule is not yet out.
findings.independence: Proposed rule and HGNS APC discussion confirmed by the AAO-HNS comment letter (https://www.entnet.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AAOHNS-Comments-on-CY2027-OPPS-ASC-NPRM.pdf, 2026-08-25). Precedent of a Q3-call next-year outlook: https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2025/11/03/inspire-medical-insp-q3-2025-earnings-transcript .

findings.finding: Nyxoah, the only other US HGNS seller, pre-announced on 2026-10-19 Q3 US revenue of ~EUR6.7M (+29% q/q) and cut its FY2026 guide to EUR33-35M from EUR36-40M because its US ramp is slower than planned, with 447 patients in prior authorization at the start of Q4: a competitor at roughly 4% of Inspire's US quarterly revenue is taking share more slowly than its own plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No resolved INSP print turned on a competitor datapoint; Jefferies' 2025 downgrade cited competitor share gains (sold off with the guide cut).
findings.why_not_priced: Public for two weeks and INSP still drifted down 6.8% in the last five sessions, so the read-through is at most partly in the price; a fully priced read-through would have shown INSP outperforming around 10-19/10-20. Sized small because the competitor is tiny relative to Inspire and its slowness could also reflect a soft overall HGNS market (the proxy cuts both ways).
findings.independence: Proxy, not an Inspire number. Same direction as management's Q2-call comment that it saw limited impact from competitive trials (https://www.webull.com/news/15381724343198720).

findings.finding: WISeR prior authorization is still in force for HGNS in six states for Q4: the House Appropriations Committee's June 9 rider defunding WISeR sits in an unenacted FY2027 Labor-HHS bill, and the CR signed 2026-09-02 funds the government to December 11 with no WISeR prohibition shown, so no Q4 relief beyond what management already planned for ('preparing to operate in WISeR for the rest of the year').
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WISeR disruption was part of the 2026-05-04 guide cut (-12.02%); since then it has been inside the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced and inside the guide; filed because an investor hoping for WISeR repeal into 2027 gets no confirmation on the call. If the market had been counting on relief, the June rider would have registered as a catalyst; it did not.
findings.independence: House rider: https://leadingage.org/house-appropriations-committee-votes-to-end-wiser-model/ (June 2026). Whether the enacted CR carries a WISeR restriction is unverified.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-01 Inspire announced that the AMA CPT Editorial Panel approved new Category I codes for single-lead HGNS (Inspire V), effective 2028-01-01, with CMS valuation proposed July 2027 and final November 2027; the stock closed +2.05% at $70.78 that day.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Coding news drove the 2026-02-11 guide cut (-12.55%); the approval itself moved the stock +2.05% on announcement.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (+2% on the day, analyst target raises followed). Residual value only if management quantifies on the call how much of the coding overhang the code removes for 2027-28; the valuation itself is unknown until 2027.

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-08-03 with ~21% of float short (2026-06-30): +22.83% on a beat-and-raise.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is not news; it sets the asymmetry. A squeeze would only start on a positive surprise, so it amplifies the guidance finding rather than standing alone, and it is sized small.
findings.independence: Earlier settlements: Benzinga 21.4% of float on 2026-06-30 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/INSP/short-interest). Skew from the sealed baseline.

baseline_tension: The lean is modestly positive against a flat skew and a negative 5- and 20-day run-up with rising short interest: it does not follow the price, and the option market is not paying for downside. That is why p_up is 56 and not higher.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the Q3 revenue finding lands inside the guided range, so it went from +1.0 to +0.5; the guidance finding stays at +1.2 because guidance is the line this stock trades on (lesson 2).
Lesson 6 (unsourced bar): there is no published 2027 consensus, so the 2027-outlook finding was capped from +0.8 to +0.5.
Lessons 5 and 7 (positioning is not a stand-alone positive): the short-interest finding went from +0.8 to +0.5; it amplifies the guide finding rather than carrying a sign of its own.
Lessons 1 and 3 moved p_up from 57 to 56 (the facts are inferences, not unseen company numbers), so expected_move went from 2.1 to 1.8; abs_move_pct 15 and print_vs_bar +1.5 were left standing.
